cachyos/automounting-drives-at-boot.title: Automounting Drives at Boot
cachyos/automounting-drives-at-boot.content:
Part of CachyOS Wiki Notes. From the official CachyOS wiki (last updated 2026-08-27).
Automounting Drives at Boot
Prerequisite: root/sudo access.

NTFS warning: NTFS is unstable under Linux with the ntfs, ntfs3 or ntfs-3g drivers. Prefer ext4/XFS/Btrfs.

Two methods:

systemd mount files — safer; a mistake won’t stop the machine booting.
/etc/fstab — advanced; a mistake can make the system unbootable.

Find UUIDs:
lsblk -f
sudo fdisk -l
Method 1 — systemd mount unit
Mount point /home/user/games → unit file /etc/systemd/system/home-$USER-games.mount (slashes become hyphens, dashes become escape codes, in /etc/systemd/system). For odd names:
systemd-escape -p --suffix=mount "/home/grzegorz/brzęczyszczykiewicz"
Template:
[Unit]
Description=
[Mount]
What=
Where=
Type=
Options=
[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

Filled example:
[Unit]
Description=Mount games drive (/home/user/games)
[Mount]
What=UUID=4e55896f-3f1f-4bc5-aa8a-fec099689cd9
Where=/home/user/games
Type=ext4
Options=defaults,exec,rw,noatime
[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

Enable it:
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now home-$USER-games.mount
Minimal version (micro /etc/systemd/system/mnt-foo.mount):
[Unit]
Description=Mount drive
[Mount]
What=UUID=<partition UUID>
Where=/mnt/foo
Type=somefs
Options=defaults
[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

Options worth knowing: _netdev for NAS mounts, nofail for non-critical drives.
Method 2 — /etc/fstab
sudo nano /etc/fstab
(The mount point /media/windows must exist.)
UUID=08A24E90A24E81E4 /media/windows ntfs3 defaults,nofail,uid=1000,gid=1000,rw,user,exec,umask=000 0 0


defaults = rw,suid,dev,exec,auto,nouser,async
nofail = keep booting if the mount fails
uid=1000 / gid=1000 = ownership; rw; user = allow non-root mounting; exec; umask=000 = permissive
First 0 = dump (deprecated), second 0 = fsck order (root = 1, btrfs root = 0, others 0 or 2)
Short form UUID=<partition UUID> /media/foo somefs is equivalent to UUID=<partition UUID> /media/foo somefs defaults 0 0

Apply:
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo mount -a
Optional convenience symlink:
ln -s /media/windows ~/Windows

cachyos/boot-manager-configuration.title: Boot Manager Configuration
cachyos/boot-manager-configuration.content:
Part of CachyOS Wiki Notes. From the official CachyOS wiki (last updated 2026-05-22). Where each bootloader’s settings actually live. See also CachyOS Boot Managers for choosing one.
systemd-boot
Two kinds of config file: systemd-boot itself in /boot/loader/loader.conf, and one file per kernel entry in /boot/loader/entry. Loader config sets the default entry and timeout:
/boot/loader/loader.conf
default @saved
timeout 5
#console-mode keep # This option configures the resolution of the console.

Kernel command line: CachyOS provides sdboot-manage, configured in /etc/sdboot-manage.conf. Edit LINUX_OPTIONS=:
LINUX_OPTIONS="zswap.enabled=0 nowatchdog quiet splash"

Then regenerate every entry:
sudo sdboot-manage gen
rEFInd
Two config files: refind.conf in boot/efi/EFI/refind (behaviour; extensively commented) and /boot/refind_linux.conf (boot options). Kernel parameters go in “Boot using default options”:
/boot/refind_linux.conf
"Boot using default options"     "root=PARTUUID=1cb353ec-7f03-4820-8b4b-03baf53a208f rw zswap.enabled=0 nowatchdog quiet splash"

Changes to both files take effect immediately — nothing to regenerate.
GRUB
One config file: /etc/default/grub.


Hide the boot menu:
/etc/default/grub
GRUB_TIMEOUT='0'
GRUB_TIMEOUT_STYLE=hidden

Press ESC at boot for the GRUB prompt; run normal or exit to get back to the menu.


Kernel command line — edit GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT:
/etc/default/grub
GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT='nowatchdog zswap.enabled=0 quiet splash'



Every change requires:
sudo grub-mkconfig -o /boot/grub/grub.cfg


Bootable BTRFS snapshots: enabled by default since the August release. For older installs:
sudo pacman -S grub-btrfs-support
which installs scripts and hooks so snapshots appear in the GRUB menu. See Btrfs Snapshots.


Limine
Menu settings live in /boot/limine.conf (sometimes on the EFI system partition); kernel parameters in /etc/default/limine. limine.conf changes take effect as soon as you save.


Menu: timeout: 5 sets the autoboot wait; default_entry: 2 # Boot the second entry by default picks the default (entries are numbered from 1; unset = 1). If default_entry points at a directory (e.g. /+CachyOS), autoboot is disabled — it must point at a specific entry number.


Entry example uses protocol: linux, kernel_path: boot():/vmlinuz-linux-cachyos, cmdline: quiet splash root=UUID=... rw, module_path: boot():/initramfs-linux-cachyos.img; boot():/ is the root of the boot drive.


Theming: wallpaper: (BMP, PNG, JPEG) plus wallpaper_style: (stretched, tiled, centered) and backdrop: (RRGGBB) when centered; term_font: (custom font file) and term_font_scale: 2x2; term_background: (AARRGGBB).


Kernel entries are automatically managed: limine-mkinitcpio-hook uses limine-entry-tool in the background as kernels are installed/removed. Parameters are set with KERNEL_CMDLINE variables in /etc/default/limine, per default / per kernel name / for fallbacks:
/etc/default/limine
# Default parameters for most kernels
KERNEL_CMDLINE[default]="quiet splash rd.udev.log_priority=3"

# Specific parameters for the 'linux-cachyos' kernel
KERNEL_CMDLINE["linux-cachyos"]="quiet splash mitigations=off"

# Parameters for fallback entries (if generated)
# KERNEL_CMDLINE[fallback]="..."

Apply with:
sudo limine-mkinitcpio
which triggers mkinitcpio including limine-mkinitcpio-hook, landing the changes in /boot/limine.conf.


Related: Secure Boot Setup, Btrfs Snapshots, CachyOS FAQ and Troubleshooting.

cachyos/browser-hardware-acceleration.title: Browser Hardware Acceleration
cachyos/browser-hardware-acceleration.content:
Part of CachyOS Wiki Notes. From the official CachyOS wiki (last updated 2026-09-18).
Browser Hardware Acceleration
Prerequisite: a Chromium-based browser (Chrome, Brave, Ungoogled Chromium, Edge, Vivaldi) plus up-to-date Mesa (AMD/Intel) or NVIDIA drivers with Vulkan/VA-API/VDPAU.
Optional monitors: amdgpu_top (AMD), nvtop (Intel Lunar Lake), intel-gpu-tools (pre-Lunar Lake).
How the flags work
Flags live in ~/.config/[browser]-flags.conf:

Chromium — ~/.config/chromium-flags.conf
Brave — ~/.config/brave-flags.conf
Ungoogled Chromium — ~/.config/ungoogled-chromium-flags.conf

Brave/Edge/Vivaldi/Opera may additionally need the Exec= line of a .desktop file edited — copy it from /usr/share/applications/ to ~/.local/share/applications/ first.
Flow: edit the flags file (e.g. nano ~/.config/chrome-flags.conf) → paste flags → restart the browser → verify at chrome://gpu (or brave://gpu).
Verify decode is actually engaged: amdgpu_top → watch the media section during playback (0% = not engaged).
Known-good configurations (verbatim from the wiki)
AMD Radeon RX 6900 XT, Google Chrome — ~/.config/chrome-flags.conf:
--use-gl=angle
--use-angle=vulkan
--enable-features=Vulkan,VulkanFromANGLE,DefaultANGLEVulkan,AcceleratedVideoDecodeLinuxZeroCopyGL,AcceleratedVideoEncoder,VaapiIgnoreDriverChecks,UseMultiPlaneFormatForHardwareVideo

NVIDIA RTX 4090, Vivaldi — ~/.config/vivaldi-stable.conf:
--enable-features=VaapiVideoDecoder,AcceleratedVideoDecodeLinuxGL,AcceleratedVideoDecodeLinuxZeroCopyGL

or in /usr/share/applications/vivaldi-stable.desktop:
Exec=/usr/bin/vivaldi-stable --enable-features=VaapiVideoDecoder,AcceleratedVideoDecodeLinuxGL,AcceleratedVideoDecodeLinuxZeroCopyGL %U

AMD Radeon RX 550, Ungoogled Chromium — ~/.config/chromium-flags.conf:
--enable-wayland-ime
--enable-features=AcceleratedVideoDecodeLinuxGL,AcceleratedVideoDecodeLinuxZeroCopyGL,AcceleratedVideoEncoder,WaylandSessionManagement,WaylandTextInputV3,WaylandUiScale,WaylandWindowDecorations

NVIDIA RTX 5070 Ti, Brave — ~/.config/brave-flags.conf:
--enable-features=VaapiVideoDecoder,AcceleratedVideoDecodeLinuxGL,AcceleratedVideoDecodeLinuxZeroCopyGL,AcceleratedVideoEncoder,VaapiIgnoreDriverChecks

AMD RX 7700 XT, Brave (DaJRJesus) — ~/.config/brave-flags.conf:
--ignore-gpu-blocklist
--enable-gpu-rasterization
--enable-zero-copy
--enable-features=AcceleratedVideoDecodeLinuxGL,AcceleratedVideoDecodeLinuxZeroCopyGL,AcceleratedVideoEncoder,CanvasOopRasterization,VaapiIgnoreDriverChecks,UseMultiPlaneFormatForHardwareVideo

AMD RX 9070 XT, Google Chrome (naknak) — ~/.config/chrome-flags.conf:
--ignore-gpu-blocklist
--enable-gpu-rasterization
--enable-zero-copy
--use-gl=angle
--use-angle=vulkan
--enable-features=VaapiVideoDecoder,AcceleratedVideoDecodeLinuxGL,AcceleratedVideoDecodeLinuxZeroCopyGL,AcceleratedVideoEncoder,VaapiIgnoreDriverChecks,UseMultiPlaneFormatForHardwareVideo,Vulkan,VulkanFromANGLE,DefaultANGLEVulkan


--ignore-gpu-blocklist is required here: RDNA 4 may be blocklisted.

NVIDIA RTX 5090, Vivaldi (icetea) — ~/.config/vivaldi-stable.conf:
--enable-features=VaapiVideoDecoder,AcceleratedVideoDecodeLinuxGL,AcceleratedVideoDecodeLinuxZeroCopyGL,VaapiOnNvidiaGPUs,VaapiIgnoreDriverChecks
--use-gl=angle
--use-angle=gl
--disable-features=Vulkan
--ignore-gpu-blocklist
--ozone-platform=wayland

Requires libva-nvidia-driver. VaapiIgnoreDriverChecks is key on NVIDIA; AV1 decode is broken in libva-nvidia-driver 0.0.17.
NVIDIA RTX 5070, Google Chrome (pisyukaev) — ~/.config/chrome-flags.conf:
--enable-features=AcceleratedVideoDecodeLinuxGL,VaapiVideoDecoder,VaapiIgnoreDriverChecks,VaapiOnNvidiaGPUs
--ignore-gpu-blocklist

Requires libva-nvidia-driver + nvidia-utils. VaapiOnNvidiaGPUs is the critical flag — Chrome otherwise blocklists NVIDIA in vaapi_wrapper.cc.
AMD RX 7600, Brave Origin (RyuuPendragon) — ~/.config/brave-origin-flags.conf:
--ignore-gpu-blocklist
--enable-gpu-rasterization
--enable-zero-copy
--enable-features=AcceleratedVideoDecodeLinuxGL,AcceleratedVideoDecodeLinuxZeroCopyGL,AcceleratedVideoEncoder,CanvasOopRasterization,VaapiIgnoreDriverChecks,UseMultiPlaneFormatForHardwareVideo

NVIDIA RTX 5070 Ti, Vivaldi (Peek4Boo7) — ~/.config/vivaldi-stable.conf:
--enable-features=AcceleratedVideoDecodeLinuxGL,AcceleratedVideoDecodeLinuxZeroCopyGL,VaapiOnNvidiaGPUs

Driver 615.71.09 / libva-nvidia-driver 0.0.18-1.1; VaapiVideoDecoder and VaapiIgnoreDriverChecks are not required at that driver version.

The wiki page carries more community submissions than are copied here — check it for your exact GPU/browser pair rather than guessing flags.

Related: Dual GPU Setup, CachyOS Filesystems.

cachyos/btrfs-snapshots.title: Btrfs Snapshots
cachyos/btrfs-snapshots.content:
Part of CachyOS Wiki Notes. From the official CachyOS wiki (last updated 2026-07-06).

Snapshots are not backups. A snapshot is a read-only or read-write (default) copy of a subvolume at a point in time, space-efficient because it references the original data until something changes. It lives on the same disk, so it dies with the disk.


CachyOS default subvolumes: /, /root, /home, /var/cache, /var/tmp, /var/log, /srv.
Good for: recovery from breakage or corruption after updates, a misconfig that prevents boot, accidental deletion.
Not useful for: bootloader problems, hardware failure.
CachyOS ships snap-pac by default, so Snapper automatically creates snapshots before and after every pacman install, upgrade or removal.
Guidance: keep roughly 10 snapshots max, use them for recovery, and give each a meaningful description.

GUI — Btrfs Assistant
Requires btrfsmaintenance.
btrfs-assistant-launcher
sudo -E btrfs-assistant
Retention settings (root config selected): Hourly/Daily/Weekly/Monthly/Yearly = 0; untick Enable timeline snapshots; Number = 10; tick Snapper cleanup enabled; Save + Apply systemd changes → enables snapper-cleanup.timer.
Verify in /etc/snapper/configs/root; expected:
# limit for number cleanup
NUMBER_MIN_AGE="3600"
NUMBER_LIMIT="10"
NUMBER_LIMIT_IMPORTANT="10"

Delete snapshots with Btrfs Assistant’s Delete button, then regenerate bootloader entries (systemd-boot / GRUB / Limine — see Boot Manager Configuration).
CLI — Snapper
Snapper comes from openSUSE and is the underlying tool. CachyOS’s default Snapper config only covers the root subvolume (/) — other subvolumes need their own configs.
# Show the current configuration
sudo snapper get-config
 
# List snapshots and details
sudo snapper list
 
# Create a snapshot
sudo snapper create --type single --description "My Snapshot Description"
 
# Modify a snapshot
sudo snapper modify <option> <snapshot_number>
sudo snapper modify 729 --description 'My New Snapshot Description'
 
# Delete one snapshot
sudo snapper delete <snapshot_number>
 
# Delete a range
sudo snapper delete 718-721
modify options: --description/-d, --cleanup-algorithm/-c, --userdata/-u, --read-only, --read-write, --default.
snapper list columns: # (snapshot number, used by other commands), Type (single = standalone, pre = before a system change, post = after, linked to a pre snapshot), Pre # (the paired pre snapshot), Date, User, Cleanup (algorithm: number, timeline, or empty-pre-post), Description, Userdata.

Snapshot 0 cannot be deleted — it represents the current state of the filesystem.

Limine snapshot menu limit — back up first, then edit:
sudo cp /etc/limine-snapper-sync.conf /etc/limine-snapper-sync.conf.orig
sudo nano /etc/limine-snapper-sync.conf
Set MAX_SNAPSHOT_ENTRIES=10; SNAPSHOT_FORMAT_CHOICE=8 is recommended (date, time, description).

Gotcha: if a snapshot involved a kernel update, you cannot roll back to it.

GRUB users need the scripts/hooks that add snapshots to the menu:
sudo pacman -Syu grub-btrfs-support
Docs: snapper.io/manpages/snapper.html, snapper.io/manpages/snapper-configs.html, Arch Wiki Snapper.
Related: CachyOS Filesystems, CachyOS Boot Managers, Boot Manager Configuration.

cachyos/cachyos-boot-managers.title: CachyOS Boot Managers
cachyos/cachyos-boot-managers.content:
Part of CachyOS Wiki Notes. From the official CachyOS wiki (last updated 2025-12-21).
CachyOS Boot Managers
Available: systemd-boot, rEFInd, GRUB, Limine.

Warning: some MSI motherboards have UEFI firmware that is not fully spec-compliant, which causes compatibility issues with some boot managers (including GRUB and rEFInd). If affected, use systemd-boot or Limine.

Comparison highlights

Firmware support — systemd-boot: UEFI only. rEFInd: UEFI only. GRUB: UEFI and BIOS. Limine: UEFI and BIOS.
/boot filesystem — systemd-boot: whatever the firmware supports (usually FAT12/16/32), more with EFI drivers. rEFInd: firmware support plus ext2/3/4, Btrfs, ISO-9660, HFS+, NTFS. GRUB: broad (ext*, Btrfs, XFS, …). Limine: FAT12/16/32 and ISO9660.
Windows dual boot — systemd-boot auto-detects Windows Boot Manager on the same ESP; rEFInd auto-detects EFI loaders and kernels; GRUB via os-prober or manual config; Limine via limine-scan.
Btrfs snapshot integration — systemd-boot/rEFInd only via custom setups (not provided by CachyOS); GRUB via grub-btrfs-support; Limine via limine-snapper-sync (enabled by default on CachyOS with Btrfs).
Full disk encryption — systemd-boot/rEFInd/Limine: possible, root encrypted, /boot must stay unencrypted. GRUB: fully supported including encrypted /boot via cryptodisk (LUKS1/PBKDF2 only; LUKS2 is limited/needs workarounds).
Theming — systemd-boot: minimal, none. rEFInd: graphical, themeable. GRUB: classic, themeable. Limine: themeable menu with skins.
TPM PCR measured boot — built in for systemd-boot and GRUB; rEFInd and Limine can via systemd-ukify.

systemd-boot

Pro: very simple config, entries in separate files, works on some problematic MSI boards, config auto-generated on CachyOS, TPM PCRs measured during boot.
Con: no BIOS/MBR; barebones, no theming; non-firmware boot FS needs separate ESP + XBOOTLDR partitions and EFI drivers; cannot find boot images outside its own ESP/XBOOTLDR; no native Btrfs snapshot rollback (kernel images live on the boot partition) — snapshot booting only through custom setups CachyOS does not provide.

rEFInd

Fork of rEFIt.
Pro: auto-detects all OSes and kernels, little to no manual config, graphical macOS-style boot selector, great theming, optional touchscreen, reads images from EFI filesystems plus EXT4 and BTRFS (more via EFI drivers from the efifs package).
Con: no BIOS support; incompatible with some MSI boards; TPM PCRs not measured (fails the PCR0 reconstruction test) — fixable via UKI with systemd-stub (systemd-ukify) or by chainloading a bootloader that measures PCR.

GRUB

Oldest, largest feature set, most widely used.
Pro: supports nearly all Linux filesystems; abundant docs and community; supports encrypted /boot; Btrfs snapshot booting via grub-btrfs-support; supports BIOS and UEFI; themeable; TPM PCRs measured.
Con: large and complex with many FS drivers; noticeably slower than systemd-boot/rEFInd/Limine; incompatible with some MSI boards.

Limine

Modern, portable multiprotocol bootloader; reference implementation for the Limine boot protocol; supports Linux and chainloading.
Pro: multiple boot protocols (Multiboot2, Linux boot protocol); boots on UEFI and BIOS; GRUB-like theming; Btrfs snapshots through limine-snapper-sync, enabled by default on CachyOS with Btrfs.
Con: /boot must be FAT12/16/32 or ISO9660; does not auto-add a UEFI NVRAM entry — use efibootmgr manually or limine-entry-tool (preinstalled); no UFS; TPM PCRs not measured (same UKI/chainload workarounds as rEFInd).

TL;DR

GRUB — encrypted /boot, BIOS, mature Btrfs snapshots.
Limine — modern, out-of-box Btrfs snapshots, BIOS/UEFI, Windows dual boot via limine-scan.
rEFInd — polished graphical UI plus automatic multi-boot on UEFI.
systemd-boot — simplest setup, no snapshots needed; most reliable fallback for MSI UEFI quirks.

Related: Boot Manager Configuration, CachyOS Filesystems, Btrfs Snapshots.

cachyos/cachyos-downloads-and-iso-valida.title: CachyOS Downloads and ISO Validation
cachyos/cachyos-downloads-and-iso-valida.content:
Part of CachyOS Wiki Notes. From the official CachyOS wiki (last updated 2026-08-10).
Downloads and Validation
Official ISO sources

Website — cachyos.org/download
SourceForge — sourceforge.net/projects/cachyos-arch/files/
CachyOS mirror — mirror.cachyos.org/ISO/

Current ISO values (as published on the page)

Version: 260809
SHA256: 959f6577f45e25ee9fd8c220fd221b08e4ea79412c7315c0f922dd6d86d5e33c
SHA256 file: mirror.cachyos.org/ISO/desktop/260809/cachyos-desktop-linux-260809.iso.sha256
Signature file: cdn77.cachyos.org/ISO/desktop/260809/cachyos-desktop-linux-260809.iso.sig


These are point-in-time values. Re-check the page before downloading — a rolling distro’s ISO changes every few weeks.

Verifying integrity (SHA256)
Always verify the ISO before installing or writing bootable media.
Windows (CMD/PowerShell as Administrator, in the folder holding both files):
# Example:
certUtil -hashfile cachyos-desktop-linux-260809.iso SHA256
Compare against the hash in the downloaded file; match → proceed.
Verifying authenticity (GPG)


Import the reference key:
gpg --keyserver hkps://keys.openpgp.org --recv-key F3B607488DB35A47


Download the ISO plus its .sig, then:
gpg --verify full_iso_name.iso.sig full_iso_name.iso


A genuine ISO returns Good signature:
gpg: Signature made dom 09 ago 2026 13:30:06 -03
gpg:                using RSA key 882DCFE48E2051D48E2562ABF3B607488DB35A47
gpg: Good signature from "CachyOS <...>" [unknown]
gpg: WARNING: This key is not certified with a trusted signature!
gpg:          There is no indication that the signature belongs to the owner.
Primary key fingerprint: 882D CFE4 8E20 51D4 8E25  62AB F3B6 0748 8DB3 5A47


Gotcha: no Good signature string, or a key ID mismatch → do not use the ISO. A bad signature means tampering or corruption; make sure the image came from a legitimate CachyOS source.

The key F3B607488DB35A47 is the same one used for the keyring fix in CachyOS FAQ and Troubleshooting.

cachyos/cachyos-faq-and-troubleshooting.title: CachyOS FAQ and Troubleshooting
cachyos/cachyos-faq-and-troubleshooting.content:
Part of CachyOS Wiki Notes. From the official CachyOS wiki (last updated 2026-10-03).
Applies to CachyOS and Arch-based distros; explicitly not a replacement for the Arch Wiki (wiki.archlinux.org/title/Main_page). The page itself warns against trusting AI-model-generated commands unverified.
Reporting bugs

GitHub CachyOS/distribution, forum discuss.cachyos.org/c/feedback/bugreports/10, Discord support channel, r/cachyos. Read the pinned support guidelines first.
Simplified man pages:

tldr git
tldr git add
Log gathering
The one-command bug report (collects dmesg, journalctl, inxi, then offers to upload to the CachyOS paste site):
sudo cachyos-bugreport.sh
Run a failing GUI program from a terminal, or capture its output:
firefox &> firefox-log.txt
Press CTRL + C after it fails to start so the output gets written.
Recently upgraded packages:
grep "\[ALPM\] upgraded" /var/log/pacman.log | tail -n 50

Priorities: debug, info, notice, warning, err, crit, alert, emerg; numeric 0=emerg, 1=alert, 2=crit, 3=err, 4=warning, 5=notice, 6=info, 7=debug.
journalctl -k reads kernel messages from the systemd journal (persistent across reboots if configured); dmesg reads the volatile kernel ring buffer (lost after reboot).

Useful journalctl invocations (from the wiki page):
journalctl
journalctl -b
journalctl -u sshd -u polkit -b -0 | grep -i "fail\|error\|denied"
journalctl -f
journalctl -u adguardhome -f
journalctl --user -u pipewire -u pipewire-pulse -u wireplumber -b 0
journalctl -u bluetooth -b 0
journalctl -u bluetooth -b -1
journalctl --since "10 minutes ago"
journalctl --since "1 hour ago"
journalctl --since "2024-01-15 14:30:00"
journalctl --since "09:00" --until "10:00"
journalctl -p err..emerg
journalctl _PID=3344
journalctl /usr/bin/firefox
Kernel messages:
journalctl -k
journalctl -k -b 0
journalctl -k -b -1
journalctl -k -f
journalctl -k | grep -i "nvidia\|amd\|intel"
journalctl -k | grep -i "usb\|pci"
journalctl -k | grep -i "memory\|ram"
journalctl -k --since "1 hour ago"
dmesg equivalents:
dmesg
dmesg -T
dmesg | less
dmesg -l err,crit,alert,emerg
Installation and live environment

The live ISO ships KDE Plasma only. It exists to install CachyOS or to run cachy-chroot for recovery — test other DEs in a VM.
Installer slow to start after “Launch Installer” = it is running calamares-online.sh, which needs internet. The script: removes old keyring files → updates Arch + CachyOS keyring packages → initializes and populates the pacman keyring → enables network time sync → checks boot type (UEFI or BIOS/MBR) to prompt for the bootloader.
Installer stuck at 33% = struggling to download packages (slow/unstable connection).

Bootloader recovery (e.g. entries gone after a BIOS update)


Boot the live ISO.


Chroot into the installed system:
sudo cachy-chroot
With BTRFS + the CachyOS preset, answer y at the prompt. For extra partitions type /boot for systemd-boot, Limine or rEFInd, or /boot/efi for GRUB. If /boot was deleted, recreate it per the install guide’s UEFI/GPT scheme. See cachy-chroot Recovery Helper.


Reinstall the bootloader (Limine example):
sudo limine-install


Reinstall the CachyOS kernel:
sudo pacman -Syu linux-cachyos linux-cachyos-headers


exit the chroot, then reboot.


Pacman troubleshooting













































ErrorCause / fixsignature is invalidOutdated mirror or broken keyring. Resync with sudo pacman -Syu, rate mirrors, or reset keyrings.404 Not FoundPackage not on the current mirror; local DB out of sync → sudo pacman -Syu, then retry.could not removeUnmanageable pacman cache file → CachyOS Hello → Troubleshooting → Clear package cache, or sudo rm -r /var/cache/pacman/pkg/*File is corrupted (invalid or corrupted package (PGP signature))Keyring problem.unable to lock databaseAnother pacman holds the lock, or a crash left db.lck.failed retrieving file … Connection timed out / Couldn't resolve host name / 526Bad/slow mirrors → sudo cachyos-rate-mirrors then sudo pacman -Syu.warning: local is newer than…Stale mirror or downgrade in repo → sudo pacman -Syuu allows downgrades.failed to commit transaction (conflicting files)Files already exist from another source; remove the conflicting files manually, then re-run.ERROR: module not found: 'nvidia', 'nvidia_modeset', …chwd always enables Early Module Loading, and NVIDIA modules may be missing for other installed kernels → sudo pacman -S nvidia.
Keyring reset sequence:
sudo rm -rf /etc/pacman.d/gnupg/
sudo pacman-key --init
sudo pacman-key --populate
 
sudo pacman-key --recv-keys F3B607488DB35A47 --keyserver keyserver.ubuntu.com
sudo pacman-key --lsign-key F3B607488DB35A47
 
sudo rm -R /var/lib/pacman/sync
If that fails, the problem is mirrors, not the keyring:
sudo cachyos-rate-mirrors
sudo pacman -Scc
Remove a stale lock file:
sudo rm /var/lib/pacman/db.lck
Example conflicting-file fix:
sudo rm /usr/lib/environment.d/10-gsk.conf
Other answers


Discord asks for an unavailable update — Discord self-updates ahead of the repos; follow the Arch Wiki’s Discord fix guide.


Slow boot — systemd-analyze blame or systemd-analyze critical-chain. If cachyos-rate-mirrors.service is the culprit, stop it running at boot:
systemctl mask cachyos-rate-mirrors
systemctl mask cachyos-rate-mirrors.timer


Name origin — after the “Cachy” scheduler, the original name of the cacULE CPU scheduler (github.com/hamadmarri/cacule-cpu-scheduler). The project started in 2020–2021 when ptr1337 was collaborating with Hamad on cacULE, and the x86-64-v3 optimized distro was named after that scheduler.


-git packages — usually update once on Monday, with exceptions.


-bin packages — precompiled binaries; they do not get the same performance optimizations as source-built CachyOS packages.


Disable the Plymouth boot animation — add kernel parameters:
plymouth.enable=0 disablehooks=plymouth

Regenerate per bootloader: systemd-boot sudo sdboot-manage gen; GRUB sudo grub-mkconfig -o /boot/grub/grub.cfg; Limine sudo limine-mkinitcpio. See CachyOS Boot Managers.


Request a package — CachyOS ships many precompiled AUR packages; request more via GitHub CachyOS/distribution/issues, the forum’s repository category, or Discord.


Security and best practices

AUR safety: understand the PKGBUILD (variables source, pkgname; functions build(), package()); verify source URLs point at official/trusted sites; review install steps and .install scripts; check the maintainer’s AUR history; verify checksums (SHA256, BLAKE2b) and PGP signatures (validpgpkeys); be extra cautious with -bin packages; read the AUR comments; never use --skipinteg or similar bypass flags; control your AUR helper (yay, paru) so it shows the PKGBUILD and diffs, or build manually with makepkg; ask whether you need the package at all; keep the system updated with sudo pacman -Syu.
GUI package managers — Pamac is known to improperly handle tasks such as corrupting system package keyrings, causing PGP signature errors that block updates. Discover (KDE) and GNOME Software Center use PackageKit: generally safe for Flatpaks, risky for system packages, and can crash mid-transaction. Recommended: pacman on the CLI; if you want a GUI, Shelly or the CachyOS Package Installer (direct pacman wrappers).

cachyos/cachyos-filesystems.title: CachyOS Filesystems
cachyos/cachyos-filesystems.content:
Part of CachyOS Wiki Notes. From the official CachyOS wiki (last updated 2026-06-12).
CachyOS Filesystems
The installer offers five: XFS, BTRFS, EXT4, ZFS, F2FS — each with its utilities preinstalled.
BTRFS is the default and recommended. “Choose it if unsure.”
XFS

Journaling filesystem by SGI (1993; ported to Linux 2001).
Pro: built for speed and extreme scalability; multiple anti-corruption technologies; resistant to fragmentation (extent-based + delayed allocation).
Con: cannot be shrunk.
Package: xfsprogs.
For: simple, fast, reliable, no advanced features.

BTRFS

Copy-on-write filesystem (created 2007, declared stable in the kernel 2013).
Pro: transparent compression — CachyOS ships ZSTD level 3 by default; snapshots (COW, so they take very little space); subvolumes; can grow or shrink; fast development.
Con: sometimes needs defrag/balance; worse on rotational drives due to fragmentation.
Package: btrfs-progs.
Default subvolume layout: @ = /, @home = /home, @root = /root, @srv = /srv, @cache = /var/cache, @tmp = /var/tmp, @log = /var/log.
For: snapshot/backup functionality plus transparent compression.

EXT4

Most commonly used Linux filesystem (stable in kernel 2008).
Pro: can be as fast or faster than XFS in some cases; huge amount of documentation; proven; can grow or shrink (shrinking is offline only and requires the FS to be unmounted).
Con: lacks many advanced features.
Package: e2fsprogs.
For: the simplest, most common choice.

ZFS

Advanced FS by Sun (2005). CDDL-licensed, so it cannot live in the Linux kernel and needs a separate module. Do not use a real-time kernel with ZFS (licensing incompatibility).
Pro: pooled storage (zpool), COW snapshots, compression, Raid-Z, ARC cache (very fast reads of frequently accessed files).
Con: complicated; ARC needs a lot of RAM to be effective; out-of-tree OpenZFS module; incompatible with real-time preemption.
Tools: the ZFS-Module (CachyOS precompiles a zfs module per kernel version) and zfs-utils.
For: advanced users who want pooled storage or ARC.

F2FS

Samsung’s Flash-Friendly File System, built for NAND flash.
Pro: flash-friendly design; transparent compression reduces writes (the space savings are not currently usable by the user); better wear leveling, longer NAND life.
Con: cannot shrink; compression savings unusable; weak fsck; downgrading to a kernel older than the one that created the FS may break things; needs a workaround with GRUB on MBR/BIOS.
Package: f2fs-tools.
For: maximizing NAND lifespan. Limine is the recommended bootloader for F2FS on MBR/BIOS (no workaround needed, unlike GRUB).

TL;DR

Default BTRFS — stable, snapshots, compression.
XFS or EXT4 — simple and fast.

Related: Btrfs Snapshots, CachyOS Boot Managers.

cachyos/cachyos-kernel-manager.title: CachyOS Kernel Manager
cachyos/cachyos-kernel-manager.content:
Part of CachyOS Wiki Notes. From the official CachyOS wiki (last updated 2025-12-22).
CachyOS Kernel Manager
Installs/manages kernels from any Arch repo, builds custom CachyOS kernels, and controls sched-ext schedulers via GUI.
Install / uninstall a kernel

Launch CachyOS Kernel Manager, tick the [] box for the desired kernel, press Execute.
Uninstall: uncheck the [] next to the installed kernel and press Execute.
Execute goes unavailable when an already-installed kernel is selected.

Configuring and building a custom kernel
Only builds CachyOS variants — it cannot build or configure a stock Arch kernel.

Click Configure, adjust settings, then Build kernel.
Built packages and cache land in ~/.cache/cachyos-km/.
After a successful build you are prompted for your sudo password to install it.

Available options: custom package name (e.g. linux-custom-cachy); scheduler (BORE, RC, RT, RT+BORE, EEVDF, BMQ); enable CachyOS config; tweak via nconfig/menuconfig/xconfig/gconfig; NUMA; Modprobed-db; KBUILD CFLAGS (-O3/-O2); performance governor as default; enable BBR3; tick rate (100/250/300/500/600/750/1000Hz); tickless mode (idle/periodic/full); preemption (Full/Voluntary/Server); transparent hugepages (Always/Madvise); DAMON; automatic CPU arch detection; CPU-arch-specific optimizations; LTO (Full/Thin/No); build ZFS module; build NVIDIA closed module; build NVIDIA open module; include vmlinux with debug info/symbols; load/save Kernel Manager presets (its own only); Kernel Patches Management (remote and local).
Sched-ext framework management
Open with the sched-ext scheduler config button in the main window. The GUI can switch between sched-ext (scx) schedulers, enable/disable the scheduler service, show the running scheduler, and set scheduler flags and profiles.
It uses scx_loader, config at /etc/scx_loader.toml. Selecting a scheduler + profile starts it with that profile and persists the config for reboots. Example (scx_bpfland with the Gaming profile):
default_sched = "scx_bpfland"
default_mode = "Gaming"
 
[scheds.scx_bpfland]
auto_mode = []
gaming_mode = ["-m", "performance"]
lowlatency_mode = ["-k", "-s", "5000", "-l", "5000"]
powersave_mode = ["-m", "powersave"]
Profiles are presets that modify scheduler flags based on proven combinations for a use case. Details in the sched-ext guide’s scheduler-guide section — see sched-ext Schedulers.

cachyos/cachyos-kernels.title: CachyOS Kernels
cachyos/cachyos-kernels.content:
Part of CachyOS Wiki Notes. From the official CachyOS wiki (last updated 2026-08-31).
CachyOS Kernels
A customized kernel: upstream enhancements, configs and patches.
Performance characteristics

Customizable PKGBUILD (GCC or Clang); Clang Thin LTO by default on linux-cachyos; distributed ThinLTO builds; AutoFDO profiling on the default kernel; kCFI with LLVM.
Timer frequency options 100/250/300/500/600/750/1000 Hz (default 1000 Hz); x86-64-v3, x86-64-v4 and AMD Zen4 builds; -fivopts / -fmodulo-sched; PREEMPT_DYNAMIC.
CPU/sched: BORE, EEVDF, BMQ schedulers; POC Selector (scx_cake-inspired fast idle CPU selector); CONFIG_CACHY (“CachyOS Sauce”); AMD P-State preferred-core + linux-next amd-pstate; RT builds with BORE; sched/wait LIFO accept().
Networking: BBRv3 TCP available as a separate module alongside BBRv1.
FS/memory: built-in ZFS with precompiled modules; NTFS fixes; MGLRU/MM tuning; NVIDIA proprietary (patched) + open modules ready in-repo; BFQ and mq-deadline improvements; ADIOS 3.2.0 multi-queue I/O scheduler; VRAM cgroup (DMEM).
Hardware: AMD ISP4 camera; Steam Deck / ROG Ally / MSI Claw (deckify) HID; T2 MacBook apple-bce in staging; ASUS patches; Lenovo WMI battery charge limiting; HP OMEN Slim/MAX via hp-wmi; HDR enabled; amdgpu_ignore_min_pcap; HDMI VRR on AMD, ALLM, passive VRR, VESA DSC from EDID; AW88399 and MAX98390 HDA side codecs.
Other: v4l2loopback by default; ACS Override for VFIO/GPU passthrough; Clear Linux and linux-next cherry-picks; unstripped dbg variant (needed for AutoFDO); Binder module enabled (Waydroid).

Variants
All ship the CachyOS Base Patchset. Each has a corresponding -lto variant built with Clang instead of GCC.

















































VariantNoteslinux-cachyosDefault, recommended. 1000Hz, Clang + ThinLTO, AutoFDO profiledlinux-cachyos-boreBORE schedulerlinux-cachyos-bmqBMQ scheduler from Project C (Alfred Chen). No sched-ext supportlinux-cachyos-deckifyDefault for handhelds; BORE + handheld patches. Other kernels are not recommended/unsupported on handheldslinux-cachyos-eevdfTweaks the default scheduler for responsivenesslinux-cachyos-ltsLatest LTS, BORE, minimally patched for stabilitylinux-cachyos-hardenedBORE + linux-hardened patchset and config; aggressive hardening that stifles performance. No sched-ext supportlinux-cachyos-rcLatest mainline (Linus’s tree); where new patchset features land firstlinux-cachyos-serverServer workloads: 300Hz tickrate, no preemption, stock EEVDFlinux-cachyos-rt-boreReal-time preemption, BORE scheduler
Package naming convention
linux-cachyos                                    # default, Clang + ThinLTO
linux-cachyos-hardened                           # GCC-built
linux-cachyos-hardened-lto                       # clang-compiled counterpart
linux-cachyos-hardened-{,lto-}headers
linux-cachyos-hardened-{,lto-}nvidia
linux-cachyos-hardened-{,lto-}nvidia-open
linux-cachyos-hardened-{,lto-}zfs
linux-cachyos-hardened-{,lto-}dbg

Prebuilt modules
ZFS and NVIDIA modules ship precompiled, so there is no rebuild per kernel update and -dkms equivalents are obsolete. Both NVIDIA closed and open modules are precompiled and patched with community/NVIDIA patches to stay compatible with the latest kernel (out-of-tree module, off upstream cadence).
FAQ

AutoFDO is only on linux-cachyos because it is expensive: build with AutoFDO+debug → create a profile by running workloads → rebuild with the profile.
The realtime kernel does not improve gaming performance: far more code is preemptible, so gaming processes get preempted frequently and give resources back.

Related: CachyOS Kernel Manager, Optimized Repositories and x86-64 Levels, sched-ext Schedulers.

cachyos/cachyos-settings-package.title: CachyOS Settings Package
cachyos/cachyos-settings-package.content:
Part of CachyOS Wiki Notes. From the official CachyOS wiki (last updated 2026-07-30).
CachyOS Settings Package
Everything below ships in the cachyos-settings package. Upstream: github.com/CachyOS/CachyOS-Settings.
Helper scripts


cachyos-bugreport.sh — writes a log file to your home directory with system info + logs, then offers to upload to the CachyOS pastebin.
sudo cachyos-bugreport.sh


DLSS Swapper — updates DLSS DLLs and presets. dlss-swapper pulls the newest DLLs/presets from the NGX Updater; dlss-swapper-dll uses DLLs already in the game directory. Proton-CachyOS has built-in upgrade functionality, and PROTON_DLSS_UPGRADE=1 must not be combined with dlss-swapper — they do the same thing and conflict.


game-performance — enables the powerprofilesctl performance profile for the target process (games or anything else) and disables the screensaver while it runs.


kerver — reports current kernel version (checks x86_64 support and CPU compiler optimizations), current I/O scheduler, and a summary of CPU / I/O / sched-ext schedulers if active.


paste-cachyos — CLI uploader to paste.cachyos.org; content must be piped in:
<command> | paste-cachyos


pci-latency — tries to reduce latency / improve performance for PCI sound cards by changing the PCI latency timer. Ships as a binary (on demand) and a systemd service (applies at boot).


sbctl-batch-sign — helper for signing the files Secure Boot needs; useful when dual booting Windows (lots of EFI files). Scans for unsigned files with sbctl verify, signs with sbctl sign when needed, and skips files belonging to Windows, GRUB, and the .mui/.dll extensions. Not compatible with Limine.


topmem — Lua script showing the top memory-consuming processes by RAM, SWAP and KSM (Kernel Same-page Merging) sharing.


zink-run — forces Zink (OpenGL over Vulkan) for the target process via environment variables; useful in Steam for games that behave better under Zink.


Overrides
An override is a config file you create to change cachyos-settings defaults without touching the originals.


sysctl — tweaks are documented in /usr/lib/sysctl.d/70-cachyos-settings.conf; copy the entry you want into a new modified file under /etc/sysctl.d/.


udev — same idea: create your own file under /etc/udev/rules.d/ with the same name as the original. List the shipped udev files with:
pacman -Ql cachyos-settings | grep udev


Related: CachyOS Kernels, General System Tweaks.

cachyos/dual-gpu-setup.title: Dual GPU Setup
cachyos/dual-gpu-setup.content:
Part of CachyOS Wiki Notes. From the official CachyOS wiki (last updated 2026-07-26).
Dual GPU Setup (hybrid graphics)
Hybrid graphics = iGPU (CPU) + dGPU working in tandem, mainly on laptops. The dGPU can sleep when idle to save power and wake on demand.
PRIME is the unifying Linux hybrid-graphics tech (NVIDIA Optimus / AMD Dynamic Switchable Graphics); PRIME Offload moves rendering between GPUs.

The closed NVIDIA driver supports PRIME from 435.17; 390xx/340xx will not work.
Avoid outdated methods: nvidia-xrun, Bumblebee (unsupported), optimus-manager.

NVIDIA: nothing to configure
In CachyOS, PRIME Offload needs no configuration — nvidia-utils + cachyos-settings suffice.
Launch a program on the NVIDIA dGPU:
__NV_PRIME_RENDER_OFFLOAD=1 __VK_LAYER_NV_optimus=NVIDIA_only __GLX_VENDOR_LIBRARY_NAME=nvidia <program>
Shorthand via nvidia-prime:
sudo pacman -S nvidia-prime
prime-run <program>
Some DX12 games need this before prime-run:
VK_DRIVER_FILES=/usr/share/vulkan/icd.d/nvidia_icd.json
Mesa pairs (AMD+AMD, AMD+Intel, Intel+Nouveau)
Set DRI_PRIME=1 before the app. Nothing else to configure.
Per-application (graphical)


Lutris → Preferences → Global Options → Display → select the GPU.


Steam → Properties → Launch options, e.g.:
prime-run %command%

Force the iGPU (Radeon example):
VK_DRIVER_FILES=/usr/share/vulkan/icd.d/radeon_icd.x86_64.json:/usr/share/vulkan/icd.d/radeon_icd.i686.json %command%



Desktop integration via switcheroo-control


KDE Plasma — needs switcheroo-control (enabled by default on CachyOS fresh installs via chwd):
sudo pacman -S switcheroo-control
sudo systemctl enable --now switcheroo-control
Then right-click the desktop entry → Properties → Application → Advanced Options → check “Run using dedicated graphics card”. Works for non-NVIDIA PRIME configs too (AMD APU + AMD dedicated).


GNOME — install switcheroo-control, right-click the icon → “Run using discrete graphics”. GNOME does not remember the choice.


Cinnamon — right-click the desktop entry → Properties → enable the relevant option; needs switcheroo-control + the service.


Related: Managing Hardware with chwd, Switching Between NVIDIA and AMD GPUs, Gaming on CachyOS.

cachyos/egl-headless-3d-acceleration.title: EGL Headless 3D Acceleration
cachyos/egl-headless-3d-acceleration.content:
Part of CachyOS Wiki Notes. From the official CachyOS wiki (last updated 2026-01-28).
EGL Headless (3D acceleration)
For guests that use OpenGL — Linux, BSD, Android — you get much better performance than software paravirtualization by translating calls from the VM straight to your GPU and back, without dedicating GPU hardware to the VM (i.e. no passthrough).
Setup
Prerequisite: the VM must be eligible for 3D acceleration and running in User Session mode — see QEMU User Session.

Open the VM in VMM and follow the wiki’s picture to add EGL Headless.
In Video Virtio, tick 3D Acceleration.

That is the entire change. The page lists no packages, systemd services, config paths, or kernel parameters — it is purely a VMM UI toggle.

cachyos/gaming-on-cachyos.title: Gaming on CachyOS
cachyos/gaming-on-cachyos.content:
Part of CachyOS Wiki Notes. From the official CachyOS wiki (last updated 2026-07-26).
Gaming on CachyOS
Prerequisite: working GPU drivers.
Essential packages live in the meta-packages cachyos-gaming-meta and cachyos-gaming-applications (CachyOS Hello → Apps/Tweaks → “Install Gaming packages” installs both).
Proton-CachyOS
Based on Proton’s bleeding-edge: Wine-staging patches, Wine Fullscreen FSR, video/audio codecs for cutscenes, umu-launcher + UMU-Protonfixes support, early game hotfixes. Disable with PROTON_NO_NTSYNC=1.
Steam launch option pattern
[env variables] [wrappers] %command% [application arguments]

Examples:
PROTON_DXVK_D3D8=1

DXVK_HUD="fps,memory,version,api"

mangohud --dlsym

gamescope -W 1680 -H 1050 -w 1280 -h 720 -S fit -F fsr --mangoapp --

__GL_SHADER_DISK_CACHE_SKIP_CLEANUP=1 prime-run game-performance %command% -dx11


Only the first %command% counts — everything after it is treated as game arguments. Never chain multiple %command% separators.

umu-launcher (Lutris / Heroic)
sudo pacman -S cachyos/umu-launcher

Lutris Runner Options: Wine version = proton-cachyos-slr or proton-cachyos-native; Use System winetricks = Disabled; Enable DXVK = Enabled. System Options: Disable Lutris Runtime = Enabled, Prefer system libraries = Enabled; env var PROTON_VERB=waitforexitandrun (optional).
Note: user-defined DXVK/VKD3D/DXVK-NVAPI versions are not applied with umu-launcher.

Anti-cheat (EAC / BattlEye)
sudo pacman -S proton-cachyos-slr
Wine-CachyOS
Standalone (Lutris / Heroic / Bottles — not for Steam). Packages: wine-cachyos (replaces system wine/wine-staging) and wine-cachyos-opt (separate location, lets versions coexist).
Options: WINE_WMCLASS="[name]", WINEUSERSANDBOX=1, WINE_NO_WM_DECORATION=1, WINE_PREFER_SDL_INPUT=1.
Strict env setup:
export PATH="/opt/wine-cachyos/bin/:$PATH"
export WINEDLLPATH="/opt/wine-cachyos/lib/wine:/opt/wine-cachyos/lib32/wine:$WINEDLLPATH"
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="/opt/wine-cachyos/lib/:/opt/wine-cachyos/lib32/:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH"
WINE=/opt/wine-cachyos/bin/wine WINEPREFIX=[your prefix] winetricks [verb]
Proton flavours
proton-cachyos (in cachyos-gaming-meta); packages proton-cachyos-native and proton-cachyos-slr (slr preferred). Also Proton-EM, dwproton, Proton-GE, plus Valve’s Proton Experimental / 11.0 / 10.0.
Common fixes


H264 codec (run once, then restart Steam normally): steam steam://unlockh264/


Steam recorder stutter (breaks the Steam Overlay): LD_PRELOAD="" %command%


Proton logging: PROTON_LOG=1 %command% → ~/steam-[AppID].log (CS2 = steam-730.log); upload to paste.cachyos.org.


Disable Steam shader pre-caching when using Proton-CachyOS/-GE/-EM: Steam → Settings → Downloads → uncheck “Allow background processing of Vulkan shaders” and “Enable Shader Pre-caching”.


NTFS: do not run Proton games from NTFS drives (unsupported by Valve).


gamescope session:
pacman -S gamescope-session-cachyos
then set it as the default session.


Lutris: arguments in Game options → Arguments; wrappers (mangohud --dlsym, game-performance) in System options → Command prefix; env vars in the Environment variables table (no = in the Key field). Logs: Output debugging info = Inherit from environment, plus PROTON_LOG=1.


Performance


Do not combine gamemode and ananicy-cpp (both modify niceness):
systemctl stop ananicy-cpp


game-performance uses power-profiles-daemon to switch to the performance profile until the game exits (and switches the active scx scheduler to its gaming profile — see sched-ext Schedulers):
game-performance %command%



Increase the maximum shader cache size
Old shaders get evicted at the default size, and big games can have >1GB of shaders — which means recompiling on every launch. Create the env file:
mkdir -p ~/.config/environment.d
touch ~/.config/environment.d/gaming.conf
micro ~/.config/environment.d/gaming.conf
Paste the vendor value:
# Increase AMD's shader cache size to 12GB
MESA_SHADER_CACHE_MAX_SIZE=12G

# Increase Nvidia's shader cache size to 12GB
__GL_SHADER_DISK_CACHE_SIZE=12000000000

Restart for it to take effect. (Credit on the wiki: psygreg’s shader booster.)
Misc

DLSS preset via launch option: dlss-swapper %command% — see CachyOS Settings Package.
Ray tracing: see the Arch Wiki Hardware_raytracing page. The NVIDIA DX12 performance drop is a driver/scheduling issue, not CachyOS; no known workaround.
GPU selection: Dual GPU Setup.

Related: General System Tweaks (NVIDIA Smooth Motion), Dual GPU Setup.

cachyos/general-system-tweaks.title: General System Tweaks
cachyos/general-system-tweaks.content:
Part of CachyOS Wiki Notes. From the official CachyOS wiki (last updated 2026-07-26). Mostly AMD-specific power tuning plus a few cross-cutting tweaks.
AMD P-State driver (amd_pstate)
CPU frequency scaling driver for modern AMD APUs/CPUs, based on Collaborative Processor Performance Control (CPPC): finer-grained frequency management and a low-latency interface for the kernel to send performance hints to hardware (legacy ACPI P-states only switch in 3 P-states).
Kernel cmdline entries per mode:

Non-Autonomous Mode — amd_pstate=passive
Guided Autonomous Mode — amd_pstate=guided
Autonomous Mode (EPP) — amd_pstate=active

AMD P-State EPP is the default when nothing is configured. Test at runtime:
echo active | sudo tee /sys/devices/system/cpu/amd_pstate/status
echo guided | sudo tee /sys/devices/system/cpu/amd_pstate/status
echo passive | sudo tee /sys/devices/system/cpu/amd_pstate/status
Modes: autonomous = platform considers only min/max performance + Energy Performance Preference; guided-autonomous = platform sets the operating performance level per workload within OS-set min/max registers; non-autonomous = the OS hands the platform the desired performance level directly.
Configuring AMD P-State EPP
Governors: powersave and performance. The page recommends powersave plus a preference.
sudo cpupower frequency-set -g powersave
sudo cpupower frequency-set -g performance
echo power | sudo tee /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/energy_performance_preference
Preferences: performance, power, balance_power, balance_performance.
AMD 3D V-Cache Optimizer
Optimizes cache scheduling on dual-CCD 3D CPUs (7950X3D, 7900X3D). Requires the BIOS CPPC option set to “Driver” so sysfs can override the mode.
echo frequency | sudo tee /sys/bus/platform/drivers/amd_x3d_vcache/AMDI0101:00/amd_x3d_mode
echo cache | sudo tee /sys/bus/platform/drivers/amd_x3d_vcache/AMDI0101:00/amd_x3d_mode

frequency (default) — tasks go to the second CCD, which clocks higher than the 3D-cache CCD.
cache — tasks go first to the higher-cache CCD; mainly profitable for games.

After switching, the preferred-core ranking should change; read it with:
grep -v /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/amd_pstate_prefcore_ranking
AMD P-State Core Performance Boost (AMD Turbo Core)
echo 0 | sudo tee /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/boost   # Disable boost for all cores
lscpu -ae                                                       # Shows AMD CPB disabled globally
echo 1 | sudo tee /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cpufreq/boost   # Enable boost on cpu0
lscpu -ae
CachyOS ships a power-profiles-daemon backporting AMD CPB support: CPB is disabled under the powersave profile, enabled under balanced or performance.
ADIOS I/O scheduler
Adaptive Deadline I/O Scheduler (firelzrd; stable branch is in the kernel): a blk-mq block-layer scheduler aiming at low-latency I/O by combining deadline scheduling with learning-based adaptive latency control. Inspired by and building on mq-deadline and Kyber — it predicts I/O completion latency from past performance and request characteristics (type, size) and uses that to adjust deadlines and batching.


Version in linux-cachyos: 3.2.0; same in linux-cachyos-rc.


Four priority tiers, Tier 0 (critical system ops) to Tier 3 (background); tunable via sysfs.


Enable temporarily (lost on reboot):
sync && echo adios | sudo tee /sys/block/<yourdrive>/queue/scheduler
Replace <yourdrive> with the real identifier (e.g. sda, sdb, nvme0n1).



Gotcha: NOT enabled by default — still under active development and testing, not considered stable for all workloads and hardware. In edge cases bugs could cause system lockups.

NVIDIA Smooth Motion (RTX 40xx & 50xx)
Driver-based AI frame interpolation: infers an extra frame between two rendered frames — an alternative for games without DLSS Frame Generation. Works for DX11, DX12 and Vulkan (DXVK and VKD3D both fine).
NVPRESENT_ENABLE_SMOOTH_MOTION=1


64-bit applications only — no 32-bit games.


Overlay conflicts → NVPRESENT_QUEUE_FAMILY=1.


Drawbacks: may add slight input lag; MangoHud reports a misleading FPS (a monitor’s built-in counter is correct); image quality below DLSS Frame Generation, artifacts in fast motion; incompatible with external frame capers (in-game caps fine); cannot be combined with DLSS Frame Generation; OpenGL needs Zink:
NVPRESENT_ENABLE_SMOOTH_MOTION=1 zink-run <command>
Zink costs performance and may glitch.


Dual GPU: set DRI_PRIME=1 to pick the NVIDIA dGPU.


Power saving
thermald
Thermal management daemon for Intel systems: monitors thermal sensors and applies cooling actions (CPU power limits, performance-state changes) before firmware throttles more aggressively. Useful on Intel laptops, convertibles, tablets, handhelds and SFF PCs exposing Intel thermal controls via /sys/class/thermal. AMD CPUs are not supported.
sudo pacman -S thermald
sudo systemctl enable --now thermald.service
systemctl status thermald.service
journalctl -u thermald.service -b
RCU Lazy
Reduces power use at idle / light load — useful for laptops and handhelds. The page states 5–10% power savings at the cost of slightly reduced performance depending on scenario. Enabled by default in linux-cachyos-deckify. Kernel cmdline:
rcutree.enable_rcu_lazy=1

NVIDIA troubleshooting — GSP firmware
GSP firmware can “in some cases” hurt performance; the 555.58.02 driver largely fixed this, but it can persist on some systems (symptoms: KDE hiccups, bad performance). Disable via /etc/modprobe.d/nvidia-gsp.conf:
options nvidia NVreg_EnableGpuFirmware=0

Then:
sudo mkinitcpio -P

Gotcha: NVIDIA’s open kernel modules are built on GSP firmware, so GSP cannot be disabled there and this option is ignored — use linux-cachyos-nvidia or nvidia-dkms. Re-test GSP after each new driver install, since NVIDIA does its QA against GSP.

Audio — enhancing laptop speakers (EasyEffects)
sudo pacman -S easyeffects
sudo pacman -S lsp-plugins-lv2
sudo pacman -S zam-plugins
sudo pacman -S calf
sudo pacman -S mda.lv2

Output tab manages effects on speaker audio; Effects tab adds/modifies them.
Community presets: download from the EasyEffects Community Presets repo → Presets → “Import preset from local storage” → select file → Load.
Custom profile: ”+” in the Presets menu → name it → Load → add effects under Output > Effects.
Convolver: add it to the chain and load a .wav impulse response for your laptop model. Gotcha: it can raise volume a lot — add a Limiter after it.
Automate startup in the app’s preferences; use PipeWire > Presets Autoloading to bind presets to output devices.
Alternative: JDSP4Linux (github.com/Audio4Linux/JDSP4Linux) for PipeWire/PulseAudio clients.

OBS Studio
Use the CachyOS obs-studio-browser package instead of stock obs-studio — it carries patches for common issues such as CUDA errors and virtual camera problems.
sudo pacman -S obs-studio-browser
# If obs-studio was installed, pacman asks whether to replace it — answer "Y".
Swap: switching from ZRam to Zswap
CachyOS uses ZRam by default; Zswap is optional. Assumes the default setup (ZRam enabled, no swap partition/file created at install).


Disable ZRam via kernel parameter: systemd.zram=0


Enable Zswap:
zswap.enabled=1 zswap.shrinker_enabled=1 zswap.compressor=lz4 zswap.max_pool_percent=30



Neutralize CachyOS’s udev rule that disables Zswap (usr/lib/udev/rules.d/30-zram.rules from github.com/CachyOS/CachyOS-Settings):
sudo touch /etc/udev/rules.d/30-zram.rules


Create a swap file for Zswap.
Btrfs:
sudo btrfs subvolume create /swap
sudo btrfs filesystem mkswapfile --size 4g --uuid clear /swap/swapfile
sudo swapon /swap/swapfile
echo "/swap/swapfile none swap defaults 0 0" | sudo tee -a /etc/fstab
(Change --size for a different size — the page’s prose says e.g. 8GB while its command uses 4g.)
Non-Btrfs:
sudo dd if=/dev/zero of=/swapfile bs=1G count=8
sudo chmod 0600 /swapfile
sudo mkswap /swapfile
echo "/swapfile none swap defaults 0 0" | sudo tee -a /etc/fstab
sudo swapon /swapfile


Add the lz4 module to /etc/mkinitcpio.conf’s MODULES array:
sudo nano /etc/mkinitcpio.conf
MODULES=(... lz4)



Rebuild the initramfs — per bootloader:
sudo sdboot-manage gen                      # systemd-boot
sudo grub-mkconfig -o /boot/grub/grub.cfg   # GRUB
sudo limine-mkinitcpio                      # Limine


Reboot.

cachyos/hyprland-setup-and-keybinds.title: Hyprland Setup and Keybinds
cachyos/hyprland-setup-and-keybinds.content:
Part of CachyOS Wiki Notes. From the official CachyOS wiki (last updated 2026-09-02).
Hyprland Setup and Keybinds
Hyprland is a Wayland compositor supporting dwindle (tiling), scrolling, master, monocle and custom layouts. It is not a full desktop environment. CachyOS dots are usable out of the box, with apps following the general system theme. Dotfiles maintained by Jinra (github.com/Jinra).
Config locations

~/.config/hypr/config — monitors.lua, variables.lua, input.lua, binds.lua, windowrules.lua, workspaces.lua, environment.lua.

monitors.lua sets up monitors (edit output values in variables.lua; get the id with hyprctl monitors, e.g. DP-1; mode looks like 1920x1080@60; scale is most likely 1).
Workspaces per monitor: define them but do not exceed 10. The wiki recommends 3 workspaces per monitor plus the gaming workspace on the primary monitor.
environment.lua is not required when using UWSM.


~/.config/uwsm — the env file for global user variables (e.g. HYPRCURSOR_THEME, XCURSOR_THEME, QT_QPA_PLATFORM).
~/.config/noctalia — config.toml holds the default configuration for cachyos-hypr-noctalia; you shouldn’t need to touch it (V5; V4 files live there but are configured through Noctalia settings).
Noctalia settings: Super+Z. Recommended: enable color templates for the apps you use; there is also a plugin store.

Notable keybinds
Mod key is Windows/Command (SUPER), changeable in binds.lua.









































































ActionBindTerminalSuper+ReturnFile managerSuper+EEditorSuper+TCalculatorSuper+CBrowserSuper+WbtopControl+Shift+EscapeNoctalia settingsSuper+ZControl centerSuper+XApp launcherSuper+SpaceLockSuper+LColor pickerSuper+PScreen capture & annotatePrintClipboard historySuper+VNotification historySuper+AWorkspaceSuper+<number>Special workspace (scratchpad)Super+S
Migrating from another DE/WM
A new user account is highly recommended; replace everything in angle brackets <> including the brackets.

sudo pacman -S cachyos-hypr-noctalia. If you hit a package conflict with another -settings package (e.g. cachyos-kde-settings), you can delete the conflicting one — they do not affect current users.
sudo useradd -m <new_user> -s /bin/fish (another shell such as /bin/zsh is fine).
sudo passwd <new_user>. If you really want the same account (highly discouraged): cp -r /etc/skel/. ~ (back up/snapshot first).
Optionally install a display manager: noctalia-greeter or sddm.

sddm: sudo pacman -Syu sddm, then systemctl disable display-manager and systemctl enable sddm.
Noctalia Greeter: sudo pacman -Syu noctalia-greeter, follow the “Setting up greetd” section of its docs, then systemctl disable display-manager and systemctl enable greetd.


Reboot and pick the Hyprland (UWSM) session from the display manager. If the shell fails to load, reboot once more.
Log in and follow the Post Setup Tasks.

Migrating v4 dots → V5 / updating dots
Changelogs: github.com/CachyOS/cachyos-hypr-noctalia/releases. Once keybinds are migrated v4 → v5, the old ones no longer work for Noctalia IPC calls.

Install meld if missing (pacman -Q meld to check).
meld /etc/skel/.config/hypr ~/.config/hypr
Blue files have changes, green files are net new.
Merge as you see fit; if you never changed a file it’s safe to overwrite it whole. Do not overwrite what you changed, such as monitor settings.
Save and exit.
Net-new green files go into ~/.config/hypr/config/ with the same name. There are 4 new files; renames: defaults.lua → variables.lua, keybinds.lua → binds.lua, input.lua → inputs.lua; workspaces.lua is new and can be moved cleanly. Custom additions must be moved by hand.

Noctalia updates:
rm -rf ~/.config/noctalia
cp -r /etc/skel/.config/noctalia ~/.config
Only config.toml matters, so it can be copied individually instead.
Removing orphans after the v4 → v5 migration:
shelly purify -o
Then reboot; if the shell fails to load, reboot once more.
FAQ

Clipboard history doesn’t survive reboots without a secrets store. Kwallet is installed by default (gnome-keyring or another store works too): install kwalletmanager, create a new wallet (blank password is easiest), then initialize it in autostart.lua with hl.exec_cmd("kwalletd6").
Dismissing satty — ctrl+s saves, ctrl+c copies. Disable it in Noctalia settings → shell → screenshot.
Change keyboard input — edit inputs.lua and add kb_layout.
Theming gaps — Cachy’s default repo only provides qt6ct; for Plasma Qt apps (dolphin, gwenview) get qt6ct-kde from the AUR.
Default browser — xdg-settings set default-web-browser your_browser.desktop (find the desktop file name with ls /usr/share/applications/).

Related: Switching Desktop Environments, CachyOS Desktop Environments.

cachyos/installing-cachyos-on-a-desktop-.title: Installing CachyOS on a Desktop or Laptop
cachyos/installing-cachyos-on-a-desktop-.content:
Part of CachyOS Wiki Notes. From the official CachyOS wiki (last updated 2026-05-20).
Installing CachyOS on a Desktop or Laptop
Before you begin

If only GRUB and Limine show up as boot manager options after Launch Installer, the system booted in Legacy/BIOS mode.
Legacy USB Support should be Auto.
Install alongside and Replace partition “are not 100% reliable and can cause the installation to fail.”
Manual partitioning is strongly preferred.
After a failed install, reboot into the ISO — the installer does not properly unmount partitions on failure, which causes continuous errors.
Secure Boot is configured post-install (separate wiki page).

Check the boot mode:
efibootmgr -v
If it prints EFI variables are not supported on this system. you booted Legacy/BIOS — enable UEFI in firmware settings.
Manual partitioning (UEFI/GPT)
Flow: Launch Installer -> Language + Region/Timezone -> Keyboard Layout -> Manual partitioning -> boot partition -> root partition -> DE -> packages -> login credentials -> summary -> Install Now. (MBR/BIOS has its own tab.)
Boot partition (step 5)

Limine: ≥ 4096 MiB, FAT32, mount /boot, flags boot.
systemd-boot & rEFInd: same parameters as Limine; the partition table varies per boot manager.
GRUB: follow the GRUB tab’s parameters.

Root partition (step 6)

Size ≥ 20000 MiB, filesystem any (see CachyOS Filesystems), mount /, no flags.

Dual booting with Windows

Not 100% reliable: Windows updates can overwrite the EFI partition and break the bootloader. Separate drives avoid this.
The EFI partition may need resizing to meet the boot manager’s minimum size.
FAT filesystems cannot be resized in place — back up the EFI filesystem, resize + reformat with something like gparted, then copy the filesystem structure back.

Windows-side prerequisites:
powercfg /H off
(Run in PowerShell as administrator — disables Fast Startup and Hibernation; reboot after.)
manage-bde -status
(Encryption Method showing None = BitLocker disabled; BitLocker must be off.)
Also required: Secure Boot disabled, a ≥30 GB empty partition (shrink a Windows partition via Win + R -> diskmgmt.msc -> right-click the main partition, usually C: -> Shrink Volume... -> at least 30720 MB), and a bootable CachyOS USB.
Limine should auto-detect the Windows EFI partition. If Windows does not appear in the boot menu:
sudo limine-scan
Related: Preparing a CachyOS USB Installer, CachyOS Boot Managers, CachyOS Desktop Environments.

cachyos/kde-plasma-on-cachyos.title: KDE Plasma on CachyOS
cachyos/kde-plasma-on-cachyos.content:
Part of CachyOS Wiki Notes. From the official CachyOS wiki (last updated 2026-08-24).
KDE Plasma on CachyOS
Short page — an X11 session note, an xorg-server note, and two FAQ items.
Missing X11 session
KDE split its development into multiple packages and the X11 session was removed from the default installation. Install it with:
sudo pacman -S plasma-x11-session kwin-x11
After installation, X11 appears as an option on the login screen.
Missing xorg-server (black screen at login)
Since the CachyOS 26.01 installer, xorg-server is no longer installed — and neither plasma-x11-session nor kwin-x11 pulls it in as a dependency. Not installing the Xorg server and its components manually results in a black screen during login.
sudo pacman -S xorg-server
FAQ
The “Emerald” look from the KDE screenshots — it is the Emerald Theme plus the Qogir Icon Theme, neither installed by default:
sudo pacman -S cachyos-emerald-kde-theme-git qogir-icon-theme
Apply both in Appearance & Style - Colors & Themes.
The login screen does not mirror the desktop — the page only points at a screenshot (kde-login-screen-settings.png); no textual steps are given.
Related: Switching Desktop Environments, CachyOS Desktop Environments.

cachyos/managing-hardware-with-chwd.title: Managing Hardware with chwd
cachyos/managing-hardware-with-chwd.content:
Part of CachyOS Wiki Notes. From the official CachyOS wiki (last updated 2026-03-22).
Managing Hardware with chwd
chwd = CachyOS Hardware Detection (github.com/CachyOS/chwd/). It installs the packages and drivers the running system needs: NVIDIA GPUs, T2 MacBooks, handhelds (Steam Deck, ROG Ally). It normally runs at install time but works post-install too.
Auto-configure (installs and configures drivers/packages so the system runs optimally):
sudo chwd -a
Install a specific profile — list them first:
chwd --list-all
Example PCI profiles and priorities from the wiki output: nouveau 18, nvidia-dkms-470xx 14, nvidia-dkms-580xx 12, nvidia-open-dkms 10, macbook-t2 9, virtualmachine 5, amd 4, intel 4, fallback 3, handheld.intel-msi-claw 2, handheld.rog-ally 2, handheld.steam-deck 2, handheld 1, broadcom-wl 1.
Install a profile:
sudo chwd -i amd
Output: > Installing amd ... then > Successfully installed amd.
Full option list, verbatim from chwd --help:
Usage: chwd [OPTIONS]
Options:
  -i, --install <profile>          Install profile
  -r, --remove <profile>           Remove profile
  -d, --detail                     Show detailed info for listings
  -f, --force                      Force reinstall
      --list-installed             List installed kernels
      --list                       List available profiles for all devices
      --list-all                   List all profiles
  -a, --autoconfigure [<classid>]  Autoconfigure
      --ai_sdk                     Toggle AI SDK profiles
      --pmcachedir <PMCACHEDIR>    [default: /var/cache/pacman/pkg]
      --pmconfig <PMCONFIG>        [default: /etc/pacman.conf]
      --pmroot <PMROOT>            [default: /]
  -h, --help                       Print help
  -V, --version                    Print version

The wiki defers to chwd --help for anything else.
Related: Switching Between NVIDIA and AMD GPUs, Dual GPU Setup.

cachyos/navigating-the-cachyos-wiki.content:
Part of CachyOS Wiki Notes. From the official CachyOS wiki (last updated 2026-01-02). This one is about using the wiki itself — metadata, but two bits are genuinely useful.
Navigating the CachyOS Wiki

The wiki is written for CachyOS-specific info, but much of it applies to Arch in general — cross-check the Arch Wiki (wiki.archlinux.org/title/Main_page) for extra context and detail.
Feedback: every page has an Edit page button at the bottom linking straight to the file on GitHub; issues go to github.com/CachyOS/wiki.
Search first: search bar at the top, right of the CachyOS logo.
Sidebars: the left sidebar is the scrollable global table of contents; the right sidebar usually shows the current page’s sections.
Interactive elements — two traps when reading or scraping the wiki:

Tabs hold related content; check every tab, or you lose half the page.
Expandable sections (e.g. “Manual Installation (Advanced)”) hide detail until clicked.


Code blocks all have a Copy to clipboard button.
Pay attention to notes, tips, warnings and cautions — the page calls them out as the place common pitfalls are documented.
Theme selector (Dark/Light/Auto) and language selector live in the header. Non-English translations exist but lag the English pages.


Practical takeaway: any automated extraction of this wiki that does not render tabs and expandables will silently miss content. That happened while building these notes — see the “Gap” callouts in this folder.
